# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** 76 years old  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c9 P35](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0035), [v4 c18 P5](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper and former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c14 P3](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0003)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008)</sub>; Keeper of the Four Winds Light  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c14 P3](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0003)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim was a tall, stooped, ungainly man with a clean-shaven, deeply lined, and bronzed face. He had a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, a square brow, a rugged mouth, and deep-set, blue eyes that could twinkle or look dreamily seaward.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)_

## Personality

Captain Jim was a simple-minded, high-souled, and cheerful man with eternal youth in his heart. He possessed a rich store of sea-faring tales and an instinctive knack for vivid storytelling. Unfailingly courteous, tolerant, and deeply sympathetic, he held a firm faith in God and the fundamental goodness of life. He harbored a passionate love for beauty and a chivalrous respect for women.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P9](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0009), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P27](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0027), [v4 c7 P14](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0014), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c17 P19](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0019)_

## Goals

- To have his life-book written and published so his memories would not be forgotten  <sub>[v4 c9 P20](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0020), [v4 c24 P36](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0036), [v4 c25 P5](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0005)</sub>

## History

Captain Jim grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, and ran away to sea as a boy. In his youth, he fell in love with 'lost Margaret,' who tragically perished at sea during a squall, a loss he mourned for the rest of his life. After decades of adventuring around the globe, he returned to Four Winds and became the keeper of the lighthouse at Four Winds Point. He befriended Gilbert and Anne Blythe when they moved into the nearby 'house of dreams.' Recognizing Owen Ford as a grandson of his old friend, the schoolmaster John Selwyn, Captain Jim collaborated with him to write a book based on his own journal of sea-faring memories. Shortly after receiving a published copy of his completed 'life-book,' Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on the volume.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P28](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0028), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012), [v4 c24 P21](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0021), [v4 c25 P5](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0005), [v4 c39 P4](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0004), [v4 c39 P25](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0025), [v4 c40 P0](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0000)_

## Background by volume

- Ran away to sea at a young age after John Selwyn's marriage  <sub>[v4 c7 P28](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0028)</sub>
- Sailed the world for decades, experiencing shipwrecks, fires, mutinies, and battles  <sub>[v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050)</sub>
- Lost his early sweetheart, Margaret, when she drifted out to sea in a dory during a storm  <sub>[v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012)</sub>
- Found Dick Moore (who turned out to be George Moore) in Havana and brought him home  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033)</sub>
- Authored a journal of his life and adventures known as his 'life-book'  <sub>[v4 c9 P20](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0020), [v4 c17 P20](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0020)</sub>

## Quotes

> There oughtn’t to be no bargaining like that among the race that knows Joseph. I’ll come when I can, and you come when you can, and so long’s we have our pleasant little chat it don’t matter a mite what roof’s over us.  <sub>[v4 c9 P1](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0001)</sub>

> If it wasn’t for our dreams they might as well bury us. How’d we stand living if it wasn’t for our dream of immortality?  <sub>[v4 c20 P7](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0007)</sub>

> There’s only the one safe compass and we’ve got to set our course by that—what it’s right to do.  <sub>[v4 c30 P7](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0007)</sub>

> I reckon that whatever the New Year brings us will be the best the Great Captain has for us—and somehow or other we’ll all make port in a good harbor.  <sub>[v4 c16 P22](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0022)</sub>

> I’m the only person living in Four Winds now that can remember the schoolmaster’s bride as she was when she come to the Island. She’s been dead this thirty year, but she was one of them women you never forget.  <sub>[v4 c7 P4](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0004)</sub>
